facts.text: South Wilton represents the earliest settled portion of the town, with Anglo-European settlement beginning in the early eighteenth century.
English colonists originally acquired the land encompassing South Wilton from the indigenous Paugussett people along the Norwalk River.
South Wilton sits in the valley of the Norwalk River, with elevations ranging from the river gage to southwestern uplands.
The Norwalk River Valley Trail traverses South Wilton, providing recreational access to various wooded tracts and meadows.
Post-World War Two development in South Wilton transitioned from one-acre housing to commercial zoning for corporate offices and manufacturing.
Riparian corridors along the Norwalk River and Comstock Brook facilitate ecological connectivity and stormwater filtration in South Wilton.
